Organic Brain Disorders

Organic brain disorders — dementia, delirium, amnesic syndromes and alcohol-related brain damage.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Differentiate delirium and dementia
  • Describe causes and features of dementia
  • Give nursing care for delirious and demented patients
  • Describe amnesic and alcohol-related brain disorders

In simple words

Organic brain disorders are mental problems caused by a disease of the brain itself. The two most important are delirium (sudden, reversible) and dementia (slow, often progressive).

Delirium versus dementia

Feature Delirium Dementia
Onset Sudden, over hours to days Slow, over months to years
Duration Fluctuates over the day Persistent
Level of consciousness Reduced, drowsy Normal
Reversibility Usually reversible Often progressive

Dementia

Type Cause
Alzheimer Degenerative disease; most common
Vascular dementia Repeated strokes
Lewy body dementia Fluctuating cognition, visual hallucinations
Frontotemporal dementia Personality and language change
Mixed Combination of causes

Features: memory loss, confusion, disorientation, language difficulty, apathy, wandering, needing help with daily living.

Delirium

  • Causes: infection, dehydration, fever, medicines, drug withdrawal, head injury
  • Features: sudden confusion, restlessness, hallucinations, reversal of sleep-wake cycle
  • Nursing: find and treat the cause; good lighting, familiar people, reassurance, safety

Amnesic and alcohol-related disorders

  • Korsakoff syndrome — severe memory impairment, confabulation
  • Wernicke encephalopathy — confusion, ataxia, eye signs; give thiamine immediately

🔴 Always rule out delirium first

Sudden confusion is often a medical problem, not a mental illness. Look for fever, urinary retention, low sodium, new medicines or pain before making a diagnosis of dementia.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Delirium is sudden, fluctuating and usually reversible.
  2. Dementia is gradual, progressive and memory loss is an early feature.
  3. Alzheimer is the most common cause of dementia.
  4. Wernicke encephalopathy is treated with thiamine.
  5. Sudden confusion in an elderly patient must trigger a medical search.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Lewy body dementia causes fluctuating cognition and visual hallucinations.
  2. Vascular dementia follows repeated strokes.
  3. Korsakoff syndrome shows confabulation.
  4. Nursing: orientation cues, routine and safe environment.
  5. Family support reduces caregiver burden and placement.

📌 Memory trick

Delirium vs dementia: delirium = days; dementia = decades.

60-second revision

  • Delirium: sudden, fluctuating, reversible; treat the cause.
  • Dementia: slow, progressive; memory loss first; Alzheimer commonest.
  • Lewy body and vascular dementia are other causes.
  • Amnesic disorders: Wernicke and Korsakoff; give thiamine.
  • Care: day refill orientation cues, safety, family support.

Test yourself

Sudden confusion in an elderly patient first suggests:

Answer: B. Sudden confusion is delirium until a medical cause is found; dementia is gradual.

The commonest cause of dementia is:

Answer: A. Alzheimer disease is the most common cause of dementia in the elderly.

Wernicke encephalopathy is treated with:

Answer: B. Wernicke encephalopathy is an emergency treated immediately with parenteral thiamine.

Confabulation is a feature of:

Answer: A. Confabulation is filling memory gaps with made-up stories, typical of Korsakoff syndrome.

Which nursing action helps a confused patient?

Answer: B. Orientation cues, a consistent person, calm routine and reassurance reduce confusion.
